newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish prosecutor demands Islamist party closure.
newsitem.headline: Turkish prosecutor demands Islamist party closure.

text.p: A leading Turkish prosecutor said on Wednesday he had demanded that the constitutional court close Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party.

"I have begun a case," prosecutor Vural Savas told Reuters. Savas, the head of one of secularist Turkey's highest judicial bodies, declined to say on what grounds he had called for the outlawing of the party.
His office in April asked judicial authorities in Egypt to question a Cairo-based reporter on alleged anti-secularist remarks made by Erbakan, when he was an opposition leader.
A prosecutor at the time told reporters any information from Egypt would be passed to the constitutional court, dominated by secularists, which would consider banning Welfare.
Welfare has been ruling in coalition with the secularist True Path Party since last June. Their alliance narrowly won an oppositon censure motion on Tuesday.
